Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve noticed several brown, greasy-looking spots on my forehead that appeared a few weeks ago, and when I tried to scrape them off they wouldn’t come away. They haven’t been painful or itchy, and they don’t seem to be changing much.

Current posterior (initial priors, based on common ED dermatologic causes):  
- Seborrheic keratosis: 0.35  
- Seborrheic dermatitis: 0.20  
- Vitiligo: 0.02  
- Bed bug bite: 0.02  
- Steven-Johnson syndrome: 0.01  
(others collectively: 0.40)

Evidence so far: “brown, greasy-looking spots on forehead,” “won’t scrape off,” “not itchy/painful,” “few weeks,” “not changing much.”  
This increases likelihood of **seborrheic keratosis** (typical ‘stuck-on,’ can’t be scraped off) vs seborrheic dermatitis (more flaky/erythematous).

Likelihood ratio (LR) for seborrheic keratosis given “stuck-on, non-scrapable, brown/greasy, stable, asymptomatic”: ~3.0
